title: Florida Safe Seas Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to prohibit feeding sharks in the exclusive economic zone off the State of Florida.
summary: Federal law already makes it illegal to put food or other substances in the water to attract sharks in the ocean zone off Hawaii and U.S. Pacific territories, unless it is for harvesting sharks or covered by an exception. This bill extends that same ban to the federal waters off Florida.
brief: Extends the existing federal shark-feeding prohibition to the exclusive economic zone off Florida.

top_lines.headline: What the Shark-Feeding Ban Does
subs: Bans putting food in the water to attract sharks, except to harvest them
Currently applies to federal waters off Hawaii and U.S. Pacific territories

top_lines.headline: What This Bill Changes
subs: Adds Florida's exclusive economic zone to the prohibition

likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Webster (R-FL) with cosponsor Soto (D-FL), the bill is a narrow bipartisan amendment extending an existing prohibition to one additional state, which limits opposition. It passed the House by voice vote, but with few cosponsors its Senate timing is uncertain.

items.main: Names the Act the “Florida Safe Seas Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Prohibition on Feeding Sharks in Exclusive Economic Zone off State of Florida

items.main: Amends Section 317 of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to add Florida to the existing shark-feeding prohibition.
items.detail: The amendment strikes 'the State' and inserts 'the States', and inserts 'and Florida' after 'Hawaii'. The underlying prohibition makes it unlawful to introduce food or other substances into the water to attract sharks for any purpose other than to harvest them, within the exclusive economic zone covered by the section. The statute's existing exceptions still apply: where the Secretary or state law finds no public health hazard or safety risk, or where the activity is part of a research program funded in whole or in part by appropriated funds.

gaps: The bill extends the shark-feeding prohibition to Florida's exclusive economic zone but does not state any penalty specific to violations off Florida, relying on the existing statute's enforcement.

The bill adds Florida to a prohibition originally written for the Pacific Ocean Area but does not address whether the section's Pacific-area exceptions translate to Atlantic and Gulf waters off Florida.
The bill bans attracting sharks by feeding but does not address other shark-attraction practices that do not involve introducing food or substances into the water.

modified: Magnuson-Stevens Act Section 317 shark-feeding prohibition coverage: exclusive economic zone off Hawaii and U.S. Pacific territories -> also includes the exclusive economic zone off Florida
